keyFindings.text: Related-section placement is not enforced: `recommendedSections` is read only inside the router branch, so a reference's `related_resources` is never required, never ordered and never checked for position. That is why `pr-state-dedup.md` can end without one, `quality-config.md` can end without one, and `ROUTER.md` can place one before sections 9-11. The rule data even downgrades the asset template's "must be last" to `recommendedSections`, so the two normative sources disagree. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:928] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:323] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-asset-template.md:166]

keyFindings.text: Required sections are checked by name, not by content: `validate_required_sections` collects `## <n>.` headers, normalizes their names, and accepts a match when every required word appears as a substring of the raw heading. `requiredSections` for a reference is only `["overview"]`, so `## 1. OVERVIEW AND CASCADE AND SPECIFICITY` satisfies it even when the section has no overview prose, no Purpose and no When to Use. keyFindings.text: The divider rule can reward the setext layout: `validate_general_structure` requires a `---` line immediately above every numbered ALL-CAPS H2, and it looks only for that line, never for a blank line between the preceding prose and the rule. A text line directly above `---` therefore satisfies the structure rule while rendering as a setext heading. The guidance compounds this: the reference template forbids duplication and fixes the intro to 1-2 sentences, but its own Section 1 duplicates Section 3's when-to-create content, and neither template says a bold-label line needs a blank line after it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:676] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:690] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-reference-template.md:86] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/skill/skill-reference-template.md:182]

keyFindings.text: The H2 checker only recognises `^## (\d+)\.\s+`, so an unnumbered H2 and a letter-suffixed H2 are invisible to it: `## 2b. SMART ROUTING` never matches, which is why the ci and skilled skill bodies pass, and `pr-state-dedup.md`'s seven unnumbered H2s are never numbered at all. When a number does match, a non-sequential value is emitted as `severity: warning`, not blocking, so the P10/P8 inversion and the I8 gap cannot fail a run. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:736] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:761] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/validate_document.py:2041]

keyFindings.text: **`OVERVIEW AND <topic>` with no overview — mechanically checkable for emptiness, partially for quality.** Add `render_overview_empty`: for every H2 whose text contains OVERVIEW, require a prose paragraph of at least 40 characters or a `### Purpose` / `### When to Use` subsection with body text before the next section; flag a heading that continues after `OVERVIEW AND` as blocking. Whether the prose is a *good* overview remains human judgment, but the current `runner-contract.md` case and the pre-fix cascade case are both caught mechanically. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/references/runner-contract.md:20] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/shared/assets/template-rules.json:321]

keyFindings.text: **Adjacent bold-label lines — mechanically checkable, high precision.** Add `render_bold_label_join`: outside fenced code, flag when two consecutive non-blank lines both start with `**Label**` and neither is a list item. On the 121-file corpus the detector found zero hits at HEAD and nine blocks in the pre-fix control, so it is a true-positive-only rule with negligible false-positive risk; make it blocking. keyFindings.text: **Duplicated content — exact duplicates checkable, semantic duplication not.** Add `render_duplicate_block` for an identical paragraph or an identical bold-label line repeated inside one section (warning), which catches the current `web-performance-and-loading.md:130` doubled support sentence and the `shell/style-guide/overview-structure-and-naming.md:170/172` repeated Evidence label. The 14-file rust boilerplate is *not* catchable this way: it is semantic sameness with different topic words, so it needs a batch-level "repeated purpose sentence" heuristic (medium precision) plus editorial review. keyFindings.text: **Numbering and item order — mechanically checkable proxies, medium precision.** Extend the H2 regex to `^## (\d+)([a-z]?)\.` and make a letter suffix or a non-sequential number blocking, which catches `## 2b.` in two skill bodies and the unnumbered run in `pr-state-dedup.md`. Add a rule-id monotonic check for `^### ([A-Z]{1,4})(\d+)\.` as a warning, which catches P10 before P8 and the missing I8. Neither proves the order matches the reader's task; a monotonic id sequence is only a proxy for authoring-history ordering. keyFindings.text: **Related Resources missing or misplaced — mechanically checkable, high precision once the template settles the rule.** Add `render_related_last`: require a related section for `reference` and `asset`, and flag any same-or-higher-level heading after it. This catches the three confirmed misplacements (`ROUTER.md` §8, `sk-code-review/SKILL.md` §8, `alignment-verification-automation.md` §5) and the two confirmed omissions (`runner-contract.md`, `quality-config.md`). The template must first be made consistent: the asset template says "must be last", the reference template does not say it, and `template-rules.json` lists it as recommended only. Make all three say required-and-last, then enforce it. keyFindings.text: **Template and guidance changes — the precondition for every mechanical check.** Rewrite the reference template's Section 1/§3 duplication into one "when to create" section; add three rules the templates currently omit: (a) a bold-label line is a list item or is followed by a blank line and body text, (b) a thematic break always has a blank line above it, (c) an overview may not be titled `OVERVIEW AND <topic>`. Add the related-last clause to the *reference* template, and make the skill template's numbered-H2 rule reject letter suffixes. Without these, a validator rule would contradict the document authors are told to copy. keyFindings.text: **What stays human.** "Items ordered by authoring history instead of reader task" at the semantic level, "misplaced content" beyond heading position, and whether an overview actually orients a reader cannot be decided by a regex. The validator can surface the proxies above; the review checklist must ask a human to read the rendered page and confirm the narrative order. ruledOutDirections.text: A purely regex-driven "authoring order" detector: section order can only be judged against a named reader task, so this iteration compares sibling files against each other and the template rather than inventing a universal order.
Treating `## Rule overrides` in `rule-overrides.md:51` as a stray heading: it sits inside a fenced example, and the fence-aware scan correctly excluded it.

Treating every `firstH2NotOverview` hit on a `SKILL.md` as a template violation: skill bodies follow a different template, so only reference and asset files were scored against the reference/asset contract.
Treating long prose lines as rendering defects: they wrap in rendered Markdown, so they were recorded as a style signal, not a finding.
`ci-workflow-standards.md:54` naming `assets/workflow-template.yml` looked like a dangling link, but the asset exists at 81 lines, so it is a valid pointer.
Scoring the ci references against the asset template's Purpose/Usage pair: they are references, not assets, so the reference template's Purpose/When to Use pair is the correct baseline.
The blank double line before `---` in two references is whitespace noise, not a rendering defect.
The three scaffold assets are YAML/JSON, not Markdown; their `#<<...>>` template directives are intentional scaffold syntax rather than rendering defects.
Searching for current bare URLs in the frontend references: all nine were repaired in the restructure, so the class is now historical in this family but live elsewhere.

Treating `frontend-practice.md:95` and `:102` (`**Layers**`, `**Web topic files**`) as adjacent bold joins: they are separated by blank lines and body text, so they render as separate label paragraphs.
Treating the `**Deeper:**` handoff lines in `web-markup-and-css.md` as orphaned labels: each closes a section with a valid link.

Treating the current `web-cascade-and-selectors.md` as still defective: the diff shows the bold-label blocks became bullet lists and the bare URLs became named links, so the file now matches the template shape.
`quality-config.md:99` looked like a stray unnumbered `## Rule overrides` heading, but it sits inside a fenced markdown example; the fence-aware scan excludes it.
Counting `SKILL.md` §8 REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES as misplaced: it is the last section of the skill body, which matches the skill template's expectation.
Looking for bare URLs or adjacent bold labels in this family: none at HEAD, because these documents use bullets and tables rather than label paragraphs.
Treating the `runner-contract.md` CLI tables as the overview: they are the section content, which is the defect, not evidence that an overview exists.
Claiming the three checklist assets lack a closing related section: their tails carry link lists under a related heading, so the omission is specific to `pr-state-dedup.md`.
Looking for adjacent bold labels in the review references: the packet uses bullets and tables, so the class is absent here.
Treating `quick-reference.md`'s `### Usage` heading as a template violation on its own: the deeper defect is the incomplete table, not the heading name.
Treating `review-core.md` §9's long Python resolver as misplaced: it is an executable contract the section names, not unrelated prose.
A file-by-file read of all 45 skilled references: the boilerplate and heading signals are dense enough to characterize the family, and reading every rule body would not change the structural verdict.

Treating the checklist assets as boilerplate: their Purpose paragraphs are specific (`This split checklist protects DTO, error, panic, unsafe-code ... boundaries`), so the boilerplate is confined to the references.

Treating the repeated `### Scope`, `### Exempted Standards` and `### What Still Applies` headings in `security-testing-and-exemptions.md` as duplication: the repeat is deliberate parallel structure for two exemption tiers, and both instances carry distinct content.

Treating the same `**Evidence**:` path in `overview-modules-and-docs.md:137` and `:155` as a duplicate paragraph: two different rules cite the same implementation file, which is legitimate shared evidence.
"Frontmatter validation catches these files": all ten frontmatter fields are present in the tested files, so the frontmatter path has nothing to report.
"The citation-drift advisory would catch it": that advisory checks file-and-line citations and never changes the exit code; it has no URL, adjacency or ordering check.
"The validator is disabled for these paths": the explicit `--type reference` run returned a real verdict, not a skip, and `valid: true` came from `blocking_errors == []`.
Looking for a hidden link checker under a different rule id: the `reference` rule block has no link or URL key, and the orchestration calls no link function.
A cross-file "same purpose sentence" rule as blocking: the rust boilerplate differs by topic word and would need fuzzy matching, which is too imprecise for a blocking gate.
A validator rule that rejects every bold-label paragraph: separate label paragraphs are legitimate; only adjacency is a rendering defect.
A validator rule that rejects every raw URL: fenced command examples and generated reports can carry them; only unfenced, unlinked prose URLs are the defect.
Trying to make "reader-task order" fully mechanical: no static analysis can know the reader's task; monotonic ids and related-last are the only defensible proxies.
